questions: Did your symptoms begin after a significant head injury?
Have you had one or more seizures?
Do you currently have weakness or loss of movement in any limb?
Did you recently undergo brain surgery?
Have you had a fever or suspected infection during this illness?
During the episodes, do you remain aware of what is happening?
Can you remember the episodes afterward?
Do the episodes involve rhythmic jerking of both arms and legs?
Have you ever bitten your tongue during an episode?
Do you lose bladder control during an episode?
Have you had two or more similar unprovoked episodes separated by at least 24 hours?
Do you experience a warning sensation, unusual smell, fear, or déjà vu immediately before an episode?
Do the episodes occur only during sleep?
Is there a family history of epilepsy?
Have you recently stopped or missed an antiseizure medication?
Do the convulsive episodes usually last longer than five minutes?
Do you keep your eyes tightly closed during an episode?
Are the limb movements irregular or out of sync rather than rhythmic?
Do you return to your usual mental state immediately after an episode?
Can someone interrupt an episode by speaking to you or gently restraining a limb?
Did your seizures first begin during adolescence or early adulthood?
Do you have brief, shock-like jerks of your arms, especially shortly after waking?
Have you ever had brief episodes of staring or unresponsiveness lasting several seconds?
Do seizures or arm jerks occur more often after sleep deprivation, alcohol use, or flashing lights?
Have you ever had similar seizures despite taking an antiseizure medication correctly?
Did the seizures begin before puberty?
Have you had any developmental or intellectual difficulties since childhood?
Have you had seizure types other than generalized convulsions, such as sudden falls, prolonged staring, or brief muscle jerks?
Do you have a close relative with generalized convulsive seizures?
Have flashing lights ever triggered a seizure?
orders: Electroencephalogram (EEG), including hyperventilation and photic stimulation.
Brain MRI with an epilepsy protocol.
Serum glucose, sodium, calcium, magnesium, renal function, and liver function tests.
Urine toxicology screen and blood ethanol level.
